- The same method gives P2 ≈ (0.5, 1.389) and Q2 ≈ (0.5, −0.457) for the pair E_BC, E_AC. Reflecting P1 and Q1 across x=1/2 gives P3 ≈ (1.146, 0.661) and Q3 ≈ (−0.453, −0.262) for the pair E_AC, E_AB.
- The two equilateral triangles from the 120° symmetry are {P1, Q2, P3} and {Q1, P2, Q3}.
  - {P1, Q2, P3} has side (12√3−4)/13 ≈ 1.291, but its edge P1P3 (at y ≈ 0.661) crosses AC, so it is excluded (Solution 3's answer).
  - {Q1, P2, Q3} has side (4+12√3)/13 ≈ 1.906. Its edge Q1Q3 lies below the x-axis, and its edges P2Q1 and P2Q3 are parallel to BC or miss ABC, so none of its edges meet ABC's edges. This is the valid triangle.
